request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

The patient had no significant medical history.

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted with symptoms of cough with phlegm, runny nose, fever, and shortness of breath. A CXR was performed, and the results showed bilateral consolidation in the basal lung. The patient was diagnosed with COVID-19 and bronchial asthma and received intravenous ceftazidime 1 gr and intravenous levofloxacin 500 mg during treatment. Symptomatic treatment with medication for asthma was also administered.

Clinical Course:
The patient's symptoms significantly improved during hospitalization. The patient remained afebrile, and shortness of breath was significantly reduced. The patient's cough and runny nose also improved.

Follow-up:
The patient was advised to self-isolate at home and to continue monitoring her symptoms. Follow-up care was coordinated with the patient's primary care physician for further management.

Signed,
[Redacted]

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
In ICD-10-AM, COVID-19 is coded U07.1 (virus identified) or U07.2 (virus not identified). The question asks for a letter plus two digits, and U07 is a valid three-character category.

The clinical picture is COVID-19 with pneumonia: bilateral basal consolidation on CXR, treated with antibiotics. In ICD-10-AM, COVID-19 pneumonia is coded U07.1 as the principal diagnosis, with J12.82 as an additional code. An asthma exacerbation is a possible alternative, but the episode is driven by the COVID-19 pneumonia and the infection, so U07 is the better choice.

The prompt's chapter list does not include U, but that list is not exhaustive, and the instruction says to choose the code that fits the condition. The Australian rules place U07.1 first, so the answer is U07.

CODE: U07
